chapter_theme: One song at Uttarakosamangai (உத்தரகோசமங்கை): bowing first to Ganapati of the many sweets, the poet asks to sing Murugan's praise and so gain Siva's state, the vast space of knowledge and the nectar of refuge; the praise is a battle scene.

982.reading: The poet hails Murugan as younger brother of the elephant god of wish-granting knowledge, lord of the bhuta host, who ate sugarcane, jaggery, sugar, milk, honey, tender coconut, the three fruits and lentils into his belly, and asks whether, bowing at the golden feet and naming the peacock and the jingling anklets with melting heart, he will sing that golden praise and gain Siva's state, the great open space of knowledge, and the nectar of refuge. The praise is a battle scene in drum syllables, horses and elephants heaped up, demons' corpses covering the directions and blood like red cloud, ending with the gods regaining their city and Valli, the hunter girl of inner meaning and knowledge, at Uttarakosamangai.
982.nuance: The opening is a full offering-list to Ganapati, a rare frame, and Murugan is approached as his brother (தந்திக்கு இளையாய்). The goal is laid out in three steps: சிவபதம், ஞானப் பெருவெளி, and அமுது. உட்பொருள் ஞானக் குறமகள் gives Valli an allegorical title, the hunter girl who is the inner meaning of knowledge.

links.note: 982 asks to sing Murugan's praise and so gain Siva's state, the great open space of knowledge (ஞானப் பெருவெளி) and the nectar of refuge. Tirumular lists what the guru gave: the truth that he is the world, the world unknown to gods, the dancing feet, and the open space of grace in great bliss (பேரின்பத்து அருள்வெளி). Both name the goal as a vast open space reached through grace, in a stepwise list of gifts.
